verification.note: Reproduced by reading the code. mcp-server/src/__tests__/ask.test.ts:30 passes drive 'media' and line 39 expects the header {"X-Lit-Drive": "media"}. encodeURIComponent('media') is 'media', so this test passes with or without the encoding at mcp-server/src/tools/ask.ts:60. Grepping mcp-server/src for X-Lit-Drive finds no test for clip_url or clip_pasted (write.ts:418, :446). The only clip test, write.test.ts:336-349, checks the LITLOFT_VIEWER guard and makes no request. Sibling tools do have non-ASCII tests: read.test.ts:264-269 and 306-313, searchTools.test.ts:142-147 and 206-211, readDocument.test.ts:125-130. frontend/src/__tests__/driveHeaderEncoding.test.ts:18 adds mcp-server/src to ROOTS, and HEADER_VALUE at line 43 flags any value that does not start with encodeURIComponent(. ci.yml:10-14 sets no path filters on push or pull_request, so the frontend job runs on every change and would catch a plain revert. A behavioral regression that keeps the encodeURIComponent( prefix, for example encodeURIComponent applied to the wrong variable, would pass the scan and every mcp-server test.

specification_compliance: SPEC-CORE-046: every X-Lit-Drive sender in mcp-server/src (ask.ts:60, write.ts:418, write.ts:446, read.ts:337, read.ts:372, search.ts:23, video.ts:53) uses encodeURIComponent(drive).
regression_risks: The ask, clip_url and clip_pasted encoding has no behavioral test. Only the regex source scan in the frontend suite guards it, so a mistake that keeps the encodeURIComponent( prefix would not be caught.
test_coverage: ask.test.ts uses an ASCII drive ('media'), so it cannot tell an encoded header from a raw one.
No test asserts the request headers of clip_url or clip_pasted.
driveHeaderEncoding.test.ts statically scans mcp-server/src for X-Lit-Drive values that are not encoded.
